note: Bubble tea shops in London. Counted by BRAND, not branch (see theCountingProblem in data/topics/bubble-tea.json): a source naming 'T4 Paddington' and one naming 'T4 Westfield' are both T4, and the branch stays in the quote. Canonical names are ASCII so the normaliser cannot split Purcha from Pürcha or Dragon Cat Cafe from Dragon Cat Café.
knownGaps: NO JUDGED AWARD for bubble tea exists in Britain, so every source here is editorial, blog or video. The source-mix floor is three social voices; five YouTube channels are recorded.

TIER E (Reddit) cannot be read in this environment. Two r/london threads surfaced in search - 'Where's the best Bubble Tea in London?' (sh5sk3) and 'Best and worst boba places?' (wibjls) - and are worth recording if the user can paste them.

TIKTOK collected 14 Sep 2026: three Apify searches ('best bubble tea london', 'london boba ranking', 'bubble tea chinatown london'), 30 posts, free-plan cap of 10 per run. Ten creators recorded, ten posts declined (five for disclosed invites/gifts/paid promos). Raw results were cached in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

CHURN IS HIGH. Several lists are 2022-2023 and the Standard itself reported Biju's Soho and Camden sites and Dragon Cat's first Hammersmith site closed. The Infatuation marks Gong Cha Goodge Street permanently closed. Every name needs a trading check before print.

sources.name: Time Out - The best places to try bubble tea in London
sources.note: RANKED 1-10, dated 6 March 2026, by Alice Saville. The freshest masthead list in the topic.

quotes.Xing Fu Tang: #1 of 10, Time Out. Whips up hourly batches of pearls in a huge cauldron; house special is a brown sugar milk topped with freshly blowtorched sugar.
quotes.Dragon Cat Cafe: #2 of 10, Time Out. Hammersmith spot with a cult following for not-too-sweet flavours; cream cloud tea is a speciality, plus wheelcakes and Taiwanese snacks.
quotes.Kissaten: #3 of 10, Time Out. Japanese-style Soho shop, pricier than most; housemade honey tapioca pearls, yoghurt popping pearls, order via a screen, long queues.
quotes.Cuppo Bubbo: #4 of 10, Time Out. Herne Hill cafe with more seating than most, around a giant money tree plant; freshly brewed tea, rose bubble tea with real petals, cheese crowns.
quotes.Biju Bubble Tea Room: #5 of 10, Time Out (as 'Biju'). Organic milk only, no powder, loose-leaf tea brewed to order; Earl Grey, rooibos and matcha options.
quotes.Bubbleology: #6 of 10, Time Out. London's first bubble tea shop when it opened in 2011; boozy bubble teas at the Soho bar.
quotes.Boba Coma: #7 of 10, Time Out. Leyton; South Asian flavours - kulfi, karak, rose - with Taiwanese technique, and a boba mural.
quotes.Quaker Street Coffee & Bubble Tea: #8 of 10, Time Out (as 'Quaker Street Coffee and Bubble tea'). Shoreditch cafe with coffee, bubble tea, cakes and murals by Suflo.
quotes.Cuppacha: #9 of 10, Time Out. Long line most days on Chinatown's Newport Court, nearly a decade trading; butterfly pea ombre drinks and Oreo specials.
quotes.Purcha: #10 of 10, Time Out (as 'Pürcha'). Purified mineral water and tea brewed to order; branches in Kingsway, Charing Cross and Croydon, with seating and Taiwanese fried chicken.
